text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Boris Yeltsin to travel to Helsinki by Lljushin-96 airplane on March 19 for the March 20 summit with Bill Clinton.
- Alcohol purchasing in Helsinki follows regional pattern with more spirits sold -- less wine and beer -- the further away a district is from the city centre.
- Finnish bakeries including Fazer and Cultor conquering a shrinking Estonian market.
- Rural Finland has become one huge workshop with municipalities brainstorming for projects that could qualify for EU subsidies.
- Leftist maverick politician MEP Esko Seppanen recruiting anti-EMU people to join the Leftist Alliance.
- Renovation of government's main building completed and Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen to return to an office refurbished in malachite green.
- Southern Finland's stock of roedeer is growing by some 20-30 percent a year and hunting has become possible.
- Differentiating military service time would make it possible to lay down brigades and save money, army commander General Gustaf Hagglund says.
- Banking group Merita has sold over half of its shares in Nokia in half a year, share register shows.
- Growth in fixed-term employment is slowing and the bulk of the workforce is still in full-time permanent employment, Statistics Finland says.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Savings banks won customers from commercial banks last year.
- Politically appointed trustees in mutual insurer Suomi opposing a sale of Suomi's insurance porfolio and assets to Pohjola for anything but market value.
- Companies first excitement about Intranets turning to realism.
- Finland's electronics market up nine percent in 1996, study shows.
AAMULEHTI
- Petrol price war in Tampere has brought the price below five markka per litre for the first time in two years.
- Meat processing industry has survived its first two years in the EU better than expected since feared low-price competition from abroad has not materialised, observers say.
TURUN SANOMAT
- EU environmental ministers recommend that Finland reduce its greenhouse gas emission to zero by 2010.
DEMARI
- Parliament building attracts growing number of visitors, up at nearly 20,000 last year compared to 7,000 in 1992.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Hale-Bopp comet clearly visible in Finland in March and April; best view in early mornings in the eastern sky.
- Police warn of fake investment companies and expect a wave of fraud attempts aimed at private individuals.
- Presidents Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin expected to bring their own cars to Helsinki for their summit on March 20.
- Wingsailing, a sort of ice-yachting on snowboards or windsurfing on ice, is this year's hippest winter sport. Finn Vesa Leskinen is reigning world champion.
